_note: Per-state page language for /bhav. A Maharashtra farmer searches बाजार भाव, not मंडी भाव, and गहू, not गेहूं. Same script, different word — so the page ranks and then loses the click to a title the searcher does not recognise as his own language. Read live and cached by mtime (services/state_lang.py): fix a wording without a deploy.
_measured: GSC 28d to 2026-09-03. Marathi queries: 99 queries, 2,709 impressions, 43 clicks = 1.59% CTR, against 0.57% site-wide — this audience converts ~3x better than average. But that number is carried almost entirely by महाडीबीटी (1,536 impr, 30 clicks), an ARTICLE. The Marathi mandi queries — अकोला सोयाबीन बाजार भाव आजचे, सोयाबीन बाजार भाव जालना, गहू बाजार भाव आजचे सोलापूर, मका बाजार भाव सोलापूर — sit at positions 6-10 and earn ZERO clicks between them. Those pages exist and rank; they just answer in the wrong dialect.
_why_only_devanagari: The 2026-08-24 decision rejected expanding into more languages, and its evidence was that 0 of 1,841 queries used any non-Devanagari Indic script. Marathi is Devanagari, so that finding never covered it — which is why this file exists and why the loader REFUSES a language whose script is not Devanagari. Tamil and Kannada are settled: they get articles, not /bhav variants. Do not add them here.
_no_new_urls: This changes what an existing page SAYS, never its address. The 23 Aug diagnosis was that the site has too many URLs, not too few — a /mr/ prefix or a ?lang= would multiply 14,000 URLs by two and make the exact problem worse. One URL, worded for the state it is about.
_grammar_rule: Templates stack nouns and never inflect. Marathi possessives and locatives are irregular and crop-dependent (गहू → गव्हाचा, not गहूचा; महाराष्ट्र → महाराष्ट्रात, not महाराष्ट्रमध्ये), and a wrong ending reads as illiterate to precisely the reader being courted. Noun-stacking is also what the searchers themselves type — 'अकोला सोयाबीन बाजार भाव आजचे' is a real query, verbatim — so the safe form and the high-demand form are the same form. Keep it that way when editing.
_placeholders: {crop} {en} {place} {district} {district_en} {en_d} {state} {state_en} {n} {n_dist} {date} {year} {avg}. Place names: {district} and {place} are ALWAYS the Devanagari spelling, {district_en} and {en_d} always the Latin one ({en_d} is empty when the two are identical, so it is only for a variant that should vanish in that case). An unknown placeholder does not raise — the variant is silently skipped and the next one is tried, so a typo costs one wording, never a page.

wa._note: WhatsApp चैनल की पोस्ट — the tone and format wordings for services/wa_style. Keys are <tone>.<slot> and label.<slot>; anything absent falls back to that module's Hindi, per string, so a half-written block costs one line and never a post. NOUN-STACKED THROUGHOUT, per _grammar_rule above: no template inflects around a placeholder, because गहू becomes गव्हाचा and महाराष्ट्र becomes महाराष्ट्रात, and a wrong ending reads as illiterate to exactly the farmer this is written for. Where Hindi says '{market} की रिपोर्ट', this says '{market} — सरकारी अहवाल'.

faqs._crop_district_note: Pair 2 names {lo}/{hi}, which the caller passes ONLY when that district actually reported a min and a max. When it did not, the placeholders go unfilled, faqs() drops that pair whole, and the Marathi page shows two questions instead of three — which is the honest outcome. Never paper over it with a filler sentence: an FAQ answer that answers nothing is still an FAQ answer to Google.

mr._districts_note: Keyed on the Hindi district name _hindi_district() produces (from naksha_states.json), which is Devanagari but Hindi-spelled. Thirteen of Maharashtra's thirty-five are spelled differently in Marathi and the difference is exactly the kind the searcher types: GSC has 'गहू बाजार भाव आजचे सोलापूर' with the long ऊ, while the page said सोलापुर. The rest are identical in both languages and are omitted, the same rule the crop table follows. Two patterns dominate — the -पुर/-पूर ending, and the retroflex ळ that Hindi does not have (जळगाव, धुळे, यवतमाळ) — plus the nuqta Hindi adds and Marathi does not (गड़चिरोली, नांदेड़, रायगढ़).
mr._crops_note: Keyed on the HINDI display name, not the English commodity, because _hindi_name() has already folded every Agmarknet spelling variant onto one Hindi string by the time this is called — so one entry here covers 'Wheat', 'Wheat(Desi)' and whatever the feed invents next. A crop absent from this table keeps its Hindi name, which a Marathi reader still understands; a crop translated WRONG does not. Names identical in both languages (गाजर, पालक, मसूर, सोयाबीन) are deliberately omitted — the fallback already returns them unchanged.
mr._omitted_on_purpose: धनिया. Marathi splits what Hindi merges: कोथिंबीर is the leaf, धणे the seed, and _hindi_name() maps BOTH 'Coriander' and 'Coriander(Leaves)' to धनिया. Translating would assert 'leaf' on the seed page. Split it here only if the commodity key is ever split upstream.
